source: HackerOne Hacktivity + Google-indexed disclosures + write-up cross-reference
disclosed_date_precision_note: approximate ±6 months (derived from H1 report-ID ranges; H1 pages are JS-rendered and didn't expose dates via WebFetch)

disclosures.title: Exposed trip_no in WebSocket Responses Leading to Excessive Information Disclosure
disclosures.vector_summary: Driver sockets received trip_no before bid acceptance; trip_no fed customer tracking URLs and leaked rider PII.

disclosures.title: Broken Access Control (IDOR) in Booking Detail and Bids
disclosures.vector_summary: Authenticated user changed booking_id in GET to read other users' booking details, bids info and bids config.

disclosures.title: Ability to increase any customer offered fare (BAC)
disclosures.vector_summary: Chained unauthenticated GET /v1/config?trip_id=X to mint a hash and PUT /v1/bidding to inject a forged bid that inflated another customer's fare.

disclosures.title: Improper Access Control Allows Trip Hijacking and Passenger/Driver PII Disclosure
disclosures.vector_summary: Endpoints didn't validate trip_id ownership; attacker substituted victim's user_id in body to hijack trips and read PII.

disclosures.title: Lack of Feedback Validation Permits Cross-Trip Feedback Manipulation
disclosures.vector_summary: Auth'd passenger sent their own valid trip_id paired with any driver_id, leaving fake feedback for drivers they never rode with.

disclosures.title: IDOR on in-app hardcoded zombie endpoint
disclosures.vector_summary: Hardcoded zombie endpoint in Android app still reachable; iterating object ID exposed driver data from other users' trips.

disclosures.title: Critical Information Disclosure via /talos/api/v1/files/upload
disclosures.vector_summary: Upload pipeline buffered to local disk before S3; misconfig appended server memory chunks into uploaded files served back to clients.

disclosures.title: Customer can cancel individual trip in a batch
disclosures.vector_summary: Cancelling one trip inside a single-parcel batch left the batch in an inconsistent state; assigned partner stuck unable to complete or cancel.

summary.auth_picture: Almost everything is post-auth (rider or driver token) on root-API subdomains. No marketing-site / takeover noise.
summary.detection_difficulty_note: Most bugs require trip-lifecycle semantics knowledge. Only the legacy-endpoint IDOR (#3085742) and the file-upload memory-leak (#3228011) are remotely regex/fuzzer reachable; the rest require multi-step business-logic awareness.
summary.bounty_picture: All disclosures are $0 — Bykea operates a VRP without monetary rewards; reputation/private-invite value only.
